prov.text: Provision for Credit Losses. The provision for credit losses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $250,000, compared to $530,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the provision for credit losses reflects decreases of $6.8 million in pooled commercial construction loan balances and $14.7 million in pooled non-owner-occupied commercial real estate loan balances during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. Additionally, the decrease in the provision for credit losses includes a $99,000 decrease in net charge-offs during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.text: Non-Interest Expense. Non-interest expense was $15.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $16.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in non-interest expense is primarily attributable to a $791,000 decrease in professional fees primarily due to a decrease in legal fees, a $311,000 decrease in debit card expense and a $545,000 decrease in appraisal management fee expense due to a decrease in appraisal volume. These decreases in non-interest expense were partially offset by a $164,000 increase in occupancy expense primarily due to an increase in furniture and equipment maintenance/service contract expenses and a $261,000 increase in miscellaneous non-interest expense primarily due to an increase in deferred compensation expense associated with an increase in valuations for the assets in the deferred compensation plan and increases in various other expenses.

nonop.text: Interest expense was $5.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $6.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in interest expense is primarily due to a decrease in rates paid on interest-bearing liabilities resulting from rate decreases implemented by the FOMC from September 2025 through December 2025 and a $12.2 million decrease in time deposits from June 30, 2026 to September 30, 2026. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, average interest-bearing non-maturity deposits were $847.3 million, an increase of $80.5 million from average interest-bearing non-maturity deposits of $766.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, average certificates of deposit were $303.2 million, a decrease of $55.1 million from average certificates of deposit of $358.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The average rate paid on interest-bearing checking and savings accounts was 1.53% and 1.48% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The average rate paid on certificates of deposit was 2.82% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 3.51% for the same period one year ago.

tax.text: Income Taxes. Income tax expense was $1.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate was 22.25% for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 22.95% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Income tax expense was $4.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $3.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate was 22.21% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to 22.77% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the effective tax rate is primarily due to the North Carolina corporate income tax rate decreasing from 2.25% to 2.00% effective January 1, 2026 and the revaluation of the deferred tax asset due to further upcoming reductions in the North Carolina corporate income tax rate.

Net interest income.text: Net Interest Income. Net interest income, the major component of the Company’s net income, is the amount by which interest and fees generated by interest-earning assets exceed the total cost of funds used to carry them. Net interest income is affected by changes in the volume and mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, as well as changes in the yields earned and rates paid. Net interest margin is calculated by dividing tax-equivalent net interest income by average interest-earning assets, and represents the Company’s net yield on its interest-earning assets.

profile.name: PEOPLES BANCORP OF NORTH CAROLINA INC

intro.text: Peoples Bancorp of North Carolina, Inc. (the “Company”), was formed in 1999 to serve as the holding company for Peoples Bank (the “Bank”). The Company is a bank holding company registered with the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the “Federal Reserve”) under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended (the “BHCA”). The Company’s principal source of income is dividends declared and paid by the Bank on its capital stock, if any. The Company has no operations and conducts no business of its own other than owning the Bank and PEBK Capital Trust II. Accordingly, the discussion of the business which follows primarily concerns the business conducted by the Bank. Our principal executive offices are located at 518 West C Street, Newton, North Carolina, 28658, and our telephone number is (828) 464-5620.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
